gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a dated maker-store price comparison for the 2 × 16-inch 1920×1200 extenders. On fopomonitor.com on 2026-11-08 the FOPO S9G (Dual 16-inch, 1200P) is $299.99 and the FOPO S11 (Dual 16-inch, 1920×1200) is $399.99, so the S9G costs $100 less for the same panel format. The three-panel S788 and S788C are both $499.99.
standout_why: Compared against UPERFECT's '8 Best Triple Screen Laptop Extenders in 2026' (cited in chat ab-17). It already lists the FOPO S9G at $299.99 for Dual 16-inch 1920×1200, but gives no date or store for any price and does not list the S11, S788 or INVZI models, so the like-for-like $100 gap is not shown. FOPO's own S788, S788C and S11 pages were in the results but are rate-limited and were not readable today. The ChatGPT answers show the S11 at $399.99 and the S788 at 'about $500', but never name the S9G next to the S11 at the same resolution.
decides: This undercuts ChatGPT's pick. The S11 is $399.99 on FOPO's store and ChatGPT's own card shows the INVZI Dual Lite at $399. If the S9G is a full match (2 × 16-inch 1920×1200), it is the value pick at $299.99 and the $399 models need a reason to cost $100 more: the detachable screens on the Dual Lite, or the brightness and weight FOPO publishes for the S11. If the shopper means three extra panels, the S788 and S788C are the same price ($499.99) today, so neither costs more. Our page lists the S788C at $599.99 (2026-11-03), so that figure is now out of date. The Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro ($433.49) and other 14-inch rows don't match the 16-inch 1920×1200 request, so they lose on panel size.
